title: and everyone's heard it was Einstein who said so.
description:
and everyone's heard it was Einstein who said so. There is no real evidence Einstein ever said anything like it. The myth gets pinned on him because his name is shorthand for genius.

A broadcaster who wrote the foreword to Dale Carnegie's 'How to Win Friends and Influence People', attributing a precise '10 percent' figure to psychologist William James, who had only ever made a much vaguer claim decades earlier.

there is no dormant 90%. PET and fMRI scans show every region of the brain active to some degree at all times, even during sleep. Damage almost anywhere causes a loss of function.

Share of the body's total energy the brain burns, despite being only about 2% of its weight. Evolution should have deleted a genuinely unused 90%, not preserved it.

In 2010, MythBusters measured brain activity during a hard mental task with real medical scanners. They found up to 35% active at once, comfortably clearing the mythical 10%.

Sources:
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ten_percent_of_the_brain_myth: confirms the Einstein misattribution has no real evidential basis, the 1890s William James and Boris Sidis origin along with James's much vaguer original claim, Lowell Thomas's 1936 foreword to Dale Carnegie's book as the source of the specific '10 percent' figure pinned on James, the brain-damage and brain-scan evidence showing all regions active including during sleep, the brain's roughly 20% share of the body's energy budget against about 2% of its body weight, and the MythBusters episode of 27 October 2010 measuring up to 35% brain activity via MEG and fMRI during a complex task.
